lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Stroke.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Why time matters
sentences: With stroke, fast assessment and treatment make a big difference to how people recover.
Especially if they reach a Comprehensive Stroke Unit. That's a CSU.
Stroke Thrombolysis Services, or STS, are country hospitals with CT and acute stroke care.
And some patients can have thrombolysis, a clot-busting treatment. But only if they get there in time.

lines.head: Sugar first
sentences: First up, basic care.
Then check the blood glucose level. You're ruling out low blood sugar.
If it's below 3.5 millimoles per litre, treat it under the hypoglycaemia protocol. Then reassess.

lines.head: ROSIER
sentences: Next, do a ROSIER assessment.
It's the preferred stroke recognition tool in South Australia.
Use it alongside a good history and a thorough clinical assessment.

lines.head: Who is eligible
sentences: So who's eligible for thrombolysis? That's a Code Stroke, and every one of these has to apply.
Stroke is clinically suspected.
The ROSIER score is positive.
They were living independently before this.
They'll reach the CSU or STS within 9 hours of symptom onset.
And travel time is under 60 minutes.

lines.head: Where to go
sentences: Locally, Port Lincoln, Whyalla and Port Augusta hospitals are all Stroke Thrombolysis Services.
The Comprehensive Stroke Units are Flinders Medical Centre, the Royal Adelaide, and Lyell McEwin.
Flinders and Lyell McEwin are listed for 8 in the morning to 8 at night.

lines.head: If eligible
sentences: Eligible? Consult the EOC Clinician for authorisation to go straight to the closest CSU or STS hospital.
Request clinical support if they're unstable, or if transport's likely to take more than 20 minutes.
And confirm their ID, plus a phone number for their substitute decision maker, a close relative, or carer.

lines.head: Calling it in
sentences: Then notify the Code Stroke to the stroke coordinator. Use the SAAS Code Notification Line, or local processes.
Use ISBAR. Confirm the Code Stroke criteria, and your ETA.
On arrival, confirm it with a SAGRN notification to the receiving hospital's Emergency Department.

lines.head: Not eligible or too far
sentences: Not eligible? That's a negative ROSIER, symptoms that started more than 9 hours ago, or a patient who wasn't living independently.
Transport to the closest CSU or STS, or the nearest hospital. Or consult the EOC Clinician.
And if everything else fits, but travel's over 60 minutes, consult the EOC Clinician about transport and destination.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So. Sugar first. ROSIER next. Check the time and the distance. And call the EOC Clinician.
Now, have a go with the eligibility checker on this page.
